newsitem.title: USA: GE CAPITAL SAYS TO CUT PAINEWEBBER STAKE.
newsitem.headline: GE CAPITAL SAYS TO CUT PAINEWEBBER STAKE.

text.p: General Electric Co said Thursday it will reduce its investment in PaineWebber Group Inc to 23 percent on a diluted basis, or 15.5 million shares, from its current stake of 21.5 million shares.

The transaction, which was announced by both companies, calls for subsidiary GE Capital Services to sell PaineWebber common stock it acquired in connection with the 1994 sale of Kidder Peabody to PaineWebber.
GE Capital will continue to be represented on the PaineWebber board of directors after the sale.
PaineWebber said it plans to use the shares to fund employee stock ownership programs and for other corporate purposes.
The transaction is subject to approval by regulatory authorities.
A GE spokesman was not immediately available to comment on the reason for the sale of the shares.
